## Purpose

The FastAPI application entry point ([main.py](../../backend/app/main.py)) — process-level wiring only: logging setup,
CORS/middleware, router registration, and the app lifespan (startup restore + shutdown
teardown).

**Everything downstream (`app/api`, `app/agents`, `app/core`, `app/models`) is either imported
here or reached transitively**; nothing in the rest of the backend imports back into it.

## Shape

- [main.py](../../backend/app/main.py) — module-level logging setup runs before `FastAPI()` is constructed: a
  `_JsonFormatter` (structured JSON log lines carrying `service`/`environment`/`request_id`)
  and a `_RequestIdFilter` fed by a `contextvars.ContextVar` set per-request in
  `_request_id_middleware` (adopts nginx's `X-Request-ID` or mints one).

  `app` is built with a `lifespan` async context manager. On startup it:
  - checks the `alembic_version` table exists (refuses to boot in non-dev if the schema was
    never migrated);
  - logs the resolved LLM provider (anthropic-direct / bedrock-bearer-token / bedrock-iam);
  - wires the execution engine's resume callbacks to
    `app.api.run_engine`/`app.api.run_commands`/`app.agents.chat_narrator` — **the only site
    where the engine is handed app-layer callbacks**, since engine code never imports `app.*`
    directly;
  - calls `restore_non_terminal_runs()`;
  - starts a periodic sandbox-sweep background task.

  On shutdown it cancels the sweep task and delegates to
  `app.api.run_shutdown.shutdown_run_infrastructure()`.

  Below that, ~20 `app.include_router(...)` calls register every route group (auth, chats,
  agents, workflows, runs, run_stream, run_commands, handoff, admin, etc. — see
  `[MOD-backend-app-api](MOD-backend-app-api.md)`). A bare `GET /health` reports LLM-provider configuration.
- [__init__.py](../../backend/app/__init__.py) — empty; marks `app` as a package.

## Why this shape

All process-lifecycle concerns (logging config, DB-schema sanity check, resume-on-restart,
graceful-shutdown budget) live in one file so the boot/shutdown sequence is auditable in a
single read, but the *behavior* of each phase is delegated to dedicated modules
(`app.api.run_shutdown`, `app.agents.sandbox.sweep_expired`, the execution engine's own
`restore_non_terminal_runs`) rather than inlined — [main.py](../../backend/app/main.py) orchestrates, it does not
implement.

The engine→app callback wiring is deliberately concentrated in the lifespan startup block:
**the kernel (`agents/execution_engine`) has a standing rule of never importing `app.*`** (the
"kernel never imports app" invariant), so this is the single injection point where app-layer
persistence/WS callables are handed to the otherwise workflow-agnostic engine.

The `alembic_version` check is a dev-vs-prod fork: production refuses to serve traffic against
an unmigrated schema, while local dev only warns, so first-time contributors aren't forced
through an extra manual step.
